deviation: The draft gives the Supplier ownership of the Services, Documentation and all improvements, modifications and derivatives, with no Customer ownership of bespoke deliverables and no perpetual licence to Supplier tooling. It also adds a free-use feedback right. This breaches the playbook position that Arcadia must own bespoke deliverables, and it falls below the fallback because there is no perpetual licence. Derivatives language could capture work built from Arcadia's inputs.
suggested_text: 7.1 The Customer owns all Customer Data and all deliverables created specifically for the Customer under this Agreement ("Deliverables"), including all intellectual property rights in them. The Supplier assigns, and shall procure the assignment of, all such rights to the Customer on creation. 7.2 The Supplier retains ownership of its pre-existing tools, materials and know-how ("Supplier Tools") and grants the Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, copy and modify the Supplier Tools as incorporated in or necessary to use the Deliverables. 7.3 The Customer grants the Supplier a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence during the Term to host, copy, process and transmit Customer Data solely to provide the Services to the Customer and as needed for the purposes of Section 6. No other rights in Customer Data are granted. 7.4 Any feedback provided by the Customer may be used by the Supplier to improve its services, provided that it does not include or disclose Customer Data or Customer Confidential Information and does not identify the Customer.
